messages.content: I’m changing the Atlanta plan. I’ll go Wednesday evening, attend the Thursday workshop and Friday summit, and come home Friday. The East Point visit can wait. Please recheck the nonstop flights and compare the full cost and timing before I buy.

For Wednesday, September 17, the two useful Dallas-to-Atlanta nonstops are:

• 4:35 p.m.-7:42 p.m., $214 in standard economy
• 6:20 p.m.-9:27 p.m., $179 in basic economy or $229 in standard economy

For Friday, September 19, after the summit ends at noon:

• 3:35 p.m.-4:58 p.m., $198 basic or $248 standard
• 5:55 p.m.-7:18 p.m., $181 basic or $231 standard

All times are local. Which fare conditions and baggage should I include in the complete comparison?

One carry-on and my laptop bag, no checked bag. I need to be able to change the ticket if the summit schedule moves. Compare standard economy only, and include the seat cost if regular aisle seats aren’t free.

With those requirements, the basic fares drop out. Standard economy includes a carry-on and personal item and permits changes without a change fee, though any fare difference would apply. Regular seat selection is included on all four flights.

The 4:35 Wednesday outbound paired with the 3:35 Friday return is $462 round trip. Paired with the 5:55 return, it is $445.

The 6:20 Wednesday outbound paired with the 3:35 Friday return is $477. Paired with the 5:55 return, it is $460.

There are no mandatory baggage or seat charges, so those are the all-in airfare totals before optional upgrades.
Walk me through the practical difference between the two Wednesday arrivals. I’ll be staying downtown near the summit.

The 4:35 flight lands at 7:42 p.m. Allowing roughly 35 minutes to get off the plane and reach the MARTA station, then about 25 minutes downtown, you should reach the hotel around 8:45. That leaves time for a normal dinner and gives you some recovery before Thursday.

The 6:20 flight lands at 9:27 p.m. The same transfer puts you downtown around 10:30, with some risk of arriving later if the flight or train is delayed. It still works for Thursday’s 2:00 p.m. workshop, but it makes Wednesday mostly a travel night. The earlier flight costs $15 less when paired with the 5:55 Friday return, despite arriving sooner.
Then the earlier outbound seems obvious. Is the 3:35 Friday flight realistic, or does it create another tight airport run?

It is possible, but not relaxed. If the summit ends at noon, retrieving luggage stored at the downtown hotel could put you on MARTA around 12:40. A normal ride and airport walk would get you to security near 1:20, about 2 hours 15 minutes before departure.

That margin shrinks if the summit runs late, hotel retrieval takes time, or security is unusually slow. Leaving the hotel by 1:05 would still put you at the airport around 90 minutes before departure, which I would treat as the latest comfortable departure. The 5:55 flight adds 2 hours 20 minutes of protection and costs $17 less with the earlier outbound.
So the 4:35 Wednesday and 5:55 Friday pair is $445 total, includes both cabin bags and an aisle seat, and can be changed for a fare difference only. Correct?

Correct. The current total is $445: 4:35 p.m. Dallas to Atlanta on Wednesday and 5:55 p.m. Atlanta to Dallas on Friday, standard economy in both directions. Your carry-on and laptop bag are included, as is selection of a regular aisle seat. There is no airline change fee; if you change flights, you would pay any increase in fare, and a lower fare would be issued according to the ticket’s credit terms. The ticket is nonrefundable to the original payment method after the 24-hour cancellation window.
Before booking, compare that with the one-night Thursday option we discussed. Just airfare and schedule risk, since lodging changes separately.

The prior Thursday-to-Friday flight pair was $389, so the Wednesday-to-Friday pair is $56 more. Wednesday removes the main risk in the one-night plan: the Thursday morning flight was scheduled to reach Atlanta at 10:12 a.m. for a 2:00 p.m. workshop, leaving limited tolerance for a substantial delay. Arriving Wednesday at 7:42 p.m. gives you the entire night and Thursday morning as protection.

The Friday return risk is also lower now because the 5:55 flight leaves nearly six hours after the summit ends. For $56 more in airfare plus one additional hotel night, the Wednesday plan protects the required workshop much better.
Book the Wednesday 4:35 outbound and Friday 5:55 return in standard economy. Choose regular aisle seats in both directions, no paid upgrade.

The round trip is ticketed for $445 under confirmation ATL7Q2. You depart Dallas at 4:35 p.m. Wednesday, September 17, arrive in Atlanta at 7:42 p.m., and return Friday, September 19, at 5:55 p.m., arriving in Dallas at 7:18 p.m. Regular aisle seats 18C outbound and 20D return are assigned at no additional cost. One carry-on and one personal item are included. Changes have no airline fee, but fare differences apply; the ticket is nonrefundable after the 24-hour cancellation period.

The flight schedule now supports the Thursday workshop and Friday summit with comfortable margins. Two downtown hotel nights, September 17-19, are still unreserved, and ground transportation remains an estimate.
